To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hedonic motivation (i.e. the pleasure derived by the user from the use of internet banking) is a significant predictor of trust (i.e. confidence of the customer in the internet banking service), which in turn is a significant predictor for self efficacy (i.e. customer's belief in their capability to use internet banking) and habit (i.e. a routine behaviour of using internet banking).
the hedonic motivation, trust, self efficacy, and habit have a positive and significant relationship with behavioural intention.
hedonic motivation (H), self efficacy (SE), trust (T) habit (H) have positive influence on behavioural intention (B), which has a positive influence on internet banking adoption (A).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of HM T SE and H on BI.
the impact of hedonic motivation on internet banking intention.
the role of hedonism, self efficacy, habit and trust on behavioural intention and the intention to adopt internet banks in Pakistan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study provides an in depth and detailed analysis on the adoption of internet banking and the role of hedonistic motivation, self efficacy and habit in predicting the behavioural intention to adopt internet.
the study has successfully identified the factors that have a significant impact on individuals' intention to adopt internet bank.
the hedonic motivation, trust, self efficacy and habit of internet banking have a significant and direct impact on the behavioural intention to use internet banking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study has identified the role of trust and self-efficacy in the adoption of internet banking which has been overlooked by the previous researchers.
this study has provided an all inclusive and integrated approach for the acceptance of internet banking by incorporating existing literature.
this study is the first of its kind in Pakistan to investigate the relationship of internet banking adoption with the help of a comprehensive approach by using SEM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hedonic motivation, habit and behavioural intentions are the key factors for predicting the adoption of internet banking in Pakistan.
hedonic motivation (i.e. the enjoyment of using internet banking) has a positive effect on the adoption of internet banking in the developing country.
the adoption of internet banking can be enhanced by increasing the trust of users, their hedonic motivation and their self efficacy.
